taxonomy.note: Current Kew accepts one species in Taxodium with three varieties; Central Texas baldcypress is represented at species level here, with var. distichum as the likely local infraspecific concept.

evidence: Hays — Hays County riparian EIS and Texas State flood-recovery research document native baldcypress along perennial streams and the Blanco River.
Travis — Pace Bend Park vegetation inventory documents baldcypress-sycamore woodland in Travis County.
Williamson — county tree/plant list explicitly includes Taxodium distichum; regional Central Texas planting references also recognize it as native/adapted.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Hays and Travis are direct natural-community evidence; Williamson is retained at species-level county presence without inferring infraspecific variety.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the deciduous feathery branchlets and buttressed wet-site trunk. Baldcypress is a large deciduous conifer with flat two-ranked leaves on many lateral shoots, fibrous reddish-brown bark, round woody cones, and often knees or a swollen fluted base near water.
diagnostic_traits: feathery two-ranked leaves on many lateral shoots
foliage turns coppery and sheds in winter
swollen/fluted trunk base in wet sites
